title: Electrical Stimulation After Botulinum Toxin Injections to the Upper Extremity
brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to investigate the effectiveness of using electrical stimulation to improve upper extremity function in stroke survivors who receive botulinum toxin injections for spasticity. We hypothesize that individuals who receive the electrical stimulation could demonstrate improved benefit of the botulinum toxin injections and improved functional use of their weaker upper extremity.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of stroke, within first 6 months post stroke, have not previously received botulinum toxin injections for upper extremity spasticity, hemiplegic upper extremtity, able to communicate in English.

Exclusion Criteria:

* contraindication for electrical stimulation (presence of implanted cardiac or other medical device, open wound on the wrist or hand, malignancy), fixed contracture of the elbow, wrist or hand, inability to follow simple directions, pregnancy.
